verdict.rationale: Proa uses an islands architecture. Only components with signals and event handlers get their own small JS module plus seed state, on a shared runtime of about 1.3 KB gzipped, so the rest of the server-rendered page ships no hydration cost. That is selective, per-island hydration, but nothing documents progressive hydration itself: deferred or staged triggers such as on-visible, on-idle or priority ordering. Out-of-order Suspense streaming speeds up HTML delivery, not interactivity. Missing for 10: documented progressive or lazy hydration triggers, hydration ordering or prioritization, independent or hands-on corroboration of time-to-interactive gains.

support.subject: As a developer, I can hydrate my server-rendered app progressively so pages become interactive faster

citations.quote: Add signals and event handlers, and Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
Each hydrated RSJS island emits a small vanilla-JS module plus seed state, served with a shared runtime around 1.3 KB gzipped.
